config.title: HOC withAuth

intro.title: HOC withAuth
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Higher-Order Component (HOC) called `withAuth` that wraps other Angular components to protect them. You will learn how to use this HOC to check if a user is logged in before allowing access to a protected page. The core concept involves creating a functional HOC that returns a new component with authentication logic. You will work with Angular components, TypeScript, and conditional rendering to implement this pattern.
intro.usecase: Higher-Order Components like withAuth are essential in Angular applications that require role-based access control. You'll implement this pattern in admin dashboards to restrict certain panels to authorized users, in e-commerce checkout flows to verify authentication before payment, and in enterprise applications to conditionally render sensitive data tables or configuration forms. As a developer, you'll use withAuth to wrap route components, ensuring unauthorized users are redirected to login pages while maintaining clean separation between authentication logic and UI components.

objectives: Construct a higher-order component (HOC) that wraps Angular components with authentication logic
Configure the HOC to accept a target component and return an enhanced component with auth checks
Implement authentication state management within the HOC using Angular services
Integrate the HOC with Angular's dependency injection system to access auth services
Apply the HOC to protect specific routes by wrapping route components
Manipulate component rendering based on authentication status (show/hide, redirect)
Initialize the HOC with configurable options for different authentication scenarios

steps.title: Define the HOC function structure
steps.instruction: Create a function called withAuth that takes a component class as a parameter and returns a new component class. Place it after the UserProfileComponent.
steps.hint: In Angular, a HOC is typically a function that wraps a component. Start with: export function withAuth(Component: any) { return class extends Component {} }
steps.expectedOutcome: A withAuth function is defined that accepts a component and returns a new component class.
successCriteria: The withAuth function is created with the correct signature and returns a class that extends the input component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your withAuth function takes a component parameter and returns a class that extends it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The withAuth function structure isn't quite right. It should accept a component and return a new component class.

steps.title: Add Component decorator to the HOC
steps.instruction: Add the @Component decorator to the class returned by the withAuth function. Set the selector to 'app-auth-wrapper' and the template to '<ng-content></ng-content>'.
steps.hint: Remember to import Component from '@angular/core' if not already imported. The decorator should be placed directly above the class definition.
steps.expectedOutcome: The HOC class now has Angular metadata, making it a proper Angular component that can project content.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator is added to the AuthWrapper class with selector 'app-auth-wrapper' and template '<ng-content></ng-content>'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the decorator, but check the selector and template values. They should be exactly 'app-auth-wrapper' and '<ng-content></ng-content>'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HOC class still needs the @Component decorator with proper metadata. Review Angular component basics.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.hint: Use Angular's template syntax with *ngIf to conditionally render the wrapped component. You'll need to access the WrappedComponent parameter from the withAuth function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthWrapper class now has a template that will display the wrapped component only when the user is authenticated.
successCriteria: The AuthWrapper class includes a template with *ngIf that conditionally renders the WrappedComponent based on isAuthenticated.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Provide and use the AuthService
steps.instruction: Add AuthService to the providers array of the AppModule to make it available for dependency injection throughout the application.
steps.hint: In Angular, services must be provided at a module or component level. Add AuthService to the providers array in the @NgModule decorator of AppModule.
steps.expectedOutcome: AuthService will be available for dependency injection in the HOC and other components.
successCriteria: AuthService is added to the providers array of AppModule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a provider, but make sure it's specifically AuthService in the AppModule providers array.

steps.title: Use the wrapped component in a template
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent template, add the selector for the wrapped component (e.g., <app-user-profile>) and bind a sample input value to it using property binding.
steps.hint: Use the component selector you defined in the wrapped component's @Component decorator. Bind an input property using [propertyName]="value" syntax.

<app-greeting [name]="'Alice'"></app-greeting>
steps.expectedOutcome: The wrapped component will be rendered in the AppComponent template with a bound input value when the application runs.
successCriteria: The AppComponent template contains the wrapped component's selector with property binding for an input value.

steps.feedbackPartial: You added the component selector, but make sure to include property binding for an input value.
